chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he used to attend the archery and the horse-racing contest
ai.seo_question: Did the Imams attend archery and horse racing competitions?
ai.summary: This brief narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the permissibility and social valorization of archery and horse-racing, activities traditionally linked to military preparedness and noble character in early Islamic society. By personally attending these events, the Imam affirmed their status as legitimate leisure and training grounds, reinforcing the Shia scholarly view that such physical pursuits are commendable when performed with good intent and discipline.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that he<sup>asws</sup> used to attend the archery and the horse-racing contest’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Contest is permissible only in racing animals with Khuf (feet like camel) or Hafir (with feet like horses and the like) and in sharp-shooting.”
